note: Generated, committed and diff-gated. This construct signs nothing, so there is no keyring: every value is a pure function of the committed fixtures, and the fixture tuple is SYNTHETIC BY CONSTRUCTION (RFC 2606 `.invalid` host, all-zero account, counting-pattern digests) — it describes no real system. The three pinned hashes (both projection identities and the `valid` vector's paramsHash) are NORMATIVE EXPECTED VALUES: they define what a conforming implementation MUST compute, and the generator refuses to write if a regeneration cannot reproduce them byte-identically. They are NOT attestations about any running system, and this corpus cannot prove agreement with a non-public producer — every copy compared here is public, so all of them could move together while some other implementation differed. Closing that gap needs a signed cross-implementation parity manifest, which does not exist (NON-CLAIMS.md §S6).

vectors.name: identity-action-schema
vectors.note: hash = sha256:hex(SHA-256(UTF8(JCS(descriptor)))). `implementation` is the pinned digest of the registered adapter's emitted run() source (ADR-0006-A shape) — a within-build commitment published as an expected value, so an offline verifier recomputes the identity a signed envelope advertises instead of trusting opaque hex.

vectors.name: identity-display
vectors.note: The same artifact under kind displayProjection. The two identities MUST differ: same artifact, different role — if a construction ever collapsed them, one of the two roles would be unpinned.

vectors.name: valid
vectors.note: The gate's own conformance tuple. paramsHash is the AUTHORITY pin — the exact value the a conforming implementation must derive for this deployment.

vectors.name: accept-key-order-irrelevant
vectors.note: The same deployment serialized in reverse key order binds the SAME digest: JCS sorts keys, so the digest is a property of the deployment, not of the caller's serialization. Without this, two honest descriptions of one release would produce two grants.

vectors.name: accept-label-at-bound
vectors.note: 256 characters is the identifier bound, not 255 — the boundary accepts.

vectors.name: accept-distinct-commit
vectors.note: One character of the SHA — the revision NEXT to the reviewed one. A single-field change MUST move the digest — exact authority permits only the exact attempt.

vectors.name: accept-distinct-environment
vectors.note: A staging approval must never alias production. A single-field change MUST move the digest — exact authority permits only the exact attempt.

vectors.name: accept-distinct-image
vectors.note: One character of the artifact digest. A single-field change MUST move the digest — exact authority permits only the exact attempt.

vectors.name: accept-distinct-repository
vectors.note: A different source repository. A single-field change MUST move the digest — exact authority permits only the exact attempt.

vectors.name: accept-distinct-target
vectors.note: A different target account. A single-field change MUST move the digest — exact authority permits only the exact attempt.

vectors.name: accept-distinct-operation
vectors.note: A rollback is a DIFFERENT bound action, never a cheaper spelling of the same one. A single-field change MUST move the digest — exact authority permits only the exact attempt.

vectors.name: accept-repo-with-at-and-hex-tail
vectors.note: `@` IS a legal identifier character, so the Release line is injective only because `commit` is fixed-width and the join is parsed from the RIGHT. Two of these tuples rendering one line would mean the human authorizes one of two deployments and cannot tell which.

vectors.name: reject-commit-float-number
vectors.note: A JSON float shaped like a SHA-sized number. Refused at the BYTE BOUNDARY (the strict parser admits integers only) — one layer EARLIER than an object-API validator would refuse it, which is the fail-closed direction.

vectors.name: reject-commit-40-digit-integer
vectors.note: Forty DIGITS are not forty hex characters, and an unsafe integer is refused at the byte boundary before any field rule runs.

vectors.name: reject-commit-char-array
vectors.note: An array of 40 one-character strings is not a string.

vectors.name: reject-operation-boolean
vectors.note: A boolean is not an operation.

vectors.name: reject-repository-object
vectors.note: An object is not a repository identifier — nothing is coerced to string on this path.

vectors.name: reject-commit-39-hex
vectors.note: 39 hex is not a full SHA — a near-miss must not be a near-accept.

vectors.name: reject-commit-41-hex
vectors.note: 41 hex is not a full SHA.

vectors.name: reject-commit-uppercase
vectors.note: Uppercase is REFUSED, not normalized: an equivalence class is an attacker's choice of representative, and a normalizer on a digest path is a forgery surface.

vectors.name: reject-commit-non-hex-g
vectors.note: `g` is not a hex character.

vectors.name: reject-commit-cyrillic-homoglyph
vectors.note: U+0430 CYRILLIC SMALL A renders as `a` and is not hex — a homoglyph must not survive a charset walk.

vectors.name: reject-image-no-prefix
vectors.note: 64 bare hex without the `sha256:` prefix is not the OCI spelling.

vectors.name: reject-image-sha512-prefix
vectors.note: A different hash family is a different identity scheme, not a variant spelling.

vectors.name: reject-image-63-hex
vectors.note: 63 hex after the prefix.

vectors.name: reject-image-65-hex
vectors.note: 65 hex after the prefix.

vectors.name: reject-image-mutable-tag
vectors.note: `latest` is a mutable tag; the bound artifact must be an immutable digest or the approved image is whatever the registry says tomorrow.

vectors.name: reject-operation-not-a-member
vectors.note: `restart` is not in {deploy, rollback}; a third operation is a code change and a new reviewed identity.

vectors.name: reject-operation-case-sensitive
vectors.note: `DEPLOY` is not `deploy` — the enum is exact.

vectors.name: reject-operation-proto-string
vectors.note: A null-prototype membership table has no inherited members: `__proto__` as a VALUE is just a non-member string.

vectors.name: reject-operation-constructor-string
vectors.note: Same class: `constructor` is not an operation.

vectors.name: reject-operation-tostring-string
vectors.note: Same class: `toString` is not an operation.

vectors.name: reject-repository-space
vectors.note: A space would make the rendered Release line ambiguous — two bound tuples, one line.

vectors.name: reject-repository-newline
vectors.note: A newline can rewrite what the approver reads below it.

vectors.name: reject-environment-tab
vectors.note: A tab is a control character.

vectors.name: reject-target-nul
vectors.note: A NUL byte truncates in every C-adjacent renderer it meets.

vectors.name: reject-target-ansi-escape
vectors.note: An ANSI escape can repaint a terminal renderer over the value the human is comparing.

vectors.name: reject-repository-over-max-label
vectors.note: 257 characters — one past the bound (`accept-label-at-bound` holds the other side).

vectors.name: reject-extra-force
vectors.note: A scalar extra — the flag from the measured finding. An unrecognized own key is refused at validation, exactly like an absent or malformed field.

vectors.name: reject-extra-deployment-command
vectors.note: A string extra that would drive a side effect. An unrecognized own key is refused at validation, exactly like an absent or malformed field.

vectors.name: reject-extra-nested-object

vectors.name: reject-extra-leading-space-key

vectors.name: reject-extra-lookalike-key

vectors.name: reject-extra-junk-x
vectors.note: An arbitrary unrecognized key. An unrecognized own key is refused at validation, exactly like an absent or malformed field.

vectors.name: reject-extra-proto-lookalike
vectors.note: `__proto__x` — prototype-flavoured but just an unrecognized own key. An unrecognized own key is refused at validation, exactly like an absent or malformed field.

vectors.name: reject-extra-command-exec-argv
vectors.note: A key from ANOTHER action schema (`argv`) does not become legal here. An unrecognized own key is refused at validation, exactly like an absent or malformed field.

vectors.name: reject-extra-command-exec-cwd
vectors.note: Same class: `cwd`. An unrecognized own key is refused at validation, exactly like an absent or malformed field.

vectors.name: reject-extra-command-exec-executable
vectors.note: Same class: `executable`. An unrecognized own key is refused at validation, exactly like an absent or malformed field.

vectors.name: reject-extra-command-exec-target-env

vectors.name: reject-duplicate-commit-key
vectors.note: TWO `commit` members, different SHAs. Every mainstream JSON.parse keeps the LAST silently, so the approver-visible value and the last-writer value can disagree; the strict boundary refuses the document instead of choosing a winner.
